@graph.name: No amine tested is a better BH3 trap than TMEDA: two match its 60 °C limit, four release BH3 at room temperature
@graph.description: Is any of six alternative amine-borane adducts inert to a higher temperature than TMEDA.(BH3)2 in HBpin hydroboration?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: An amine-borane with less than 5 % product at 70 °C or above where the no-amine background is still clean.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.reaction: hydroboration of terminal alkynes and alkenes with pinacolborane in toluene (and diglyme), BH3 at 20 mol %
nrr:applicabilityConditions.tmedaLoading: one-to-one TMEDA to 'catalyst' for the headline; 0.5 to 1.0 eq extends inhibition but not completely
nrr:applicabilityConditions.temperatures: external heating-block temperatures; room temperature about 18 °C
nrr:applicabilityConditions.substratesNotCovered: carbonyl compounds, for which the TMEDA test is not compatible (SI Section S4)
nrr:applicabilityConditions.note: the limit is about the TMEDA.(BH3)2 adduct's lability, so it applies to any catalysed HBpin hydroboration that uses TMEDA inhibition as its evidence of true catalysis

nrr:cost.note: bench-scale NMR kinetics; runs are the average of two; no monetary cost reported

nrr:provenanceNotes: Table 1 is a colour grid read from the figure image; each cell is one evidence item with its row and column as locator. No per-cell yields are given in the article.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: The article makes no statement about the use of AI tools.

nrr:confidence.basis: internal positives (5a, 5b) and a clean background to 70 °C in the same grid; threshold defined

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Amine-borane adducts 5a and 5b resulted in reaction inhibition (product formation <5%) up to 60 °C ... All other amine-borane adducts resulted in product formation at room temperature and above. All of the amines tested did not offer an improvement over TMEDA.

@graph.name: Does DABCO.(BH3)2 inhibit BH3-catalysed hydroboration of phenylacetylene with HBpin, and to what temperature?
@graph.nrr:question: Does DABCO.(BH3)2 inhibit BH3-catalysed hydroboration of phenylacetylene with HBpin, and to what temperature?

nrr:effect.metric: highest temperature with less than 5 % product

positive.label: DABCO.(BH3)2 (5a) and PMDTA.(BH3)3 (5b) inhibit to 60 °C in the same grid

negative.label: HBpin and substrate with no BH3 source
negative.observed: no product at 18, 60 and 70 °C; product at 80 °C
negative.note: the no-amine-borane control row is clean to 70 °C and not clean at 80 °C, because HBpin decomposes to BH3 thermally from 80 °C; the 80 °C column therefore cannot distinguish a failed trap from background catalysis

@graph.nrr:sensitivity: inhibition is defined as less than 5 % product by 1H and 11B NMR against a 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene internal standard; yields are the average of two runs
@graph.nrr:note: inhibits to 60 °C, the same limit as TMEDA; not an improvement
@graph.nrr:informativenessReason: rule applies to negative and inconclusive findings only
